item.title: - Bhikkhus, one who delights in the earth element delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. Bhikkhus,…
item.description:
- Bhikkhus, one who delights in the earth element delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. Bhikkhus, one who delights in the water element ... one who delights in the fire element ... one who delights in the air element delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 14.35

item.title: A framework of sinews and bone, plastered with flesh and skin, The body is covered by a skin — it is not seen as it…
item.description:
A framework of sinews and bone, plastered with flesh and skin,
The body is covered by a skin — it is not seen as it really is.

Filled with a full belly: the liver, bladder, heart, lungs,
Kidneys and spleen, mucus, saliva, sweat, fat, blood, synovial fluid,
Bile, and serum.

From these nine streams, defilement constantly flows:
From the eyes, eye discharge; from the ears, ear discharge;
From the nose, nasal mucus; from the mouth, sometimes vomit,
Bile and phlegm; from the body, sweat and dirt.

From: Sutta Nipāta 1.11

item.title: ( Sakka ): Everyone should strive Until the goal is achieved. When the goal is achieved, One shines brilliantly. There is nothing better Than patience.
item.description:
( Sakka ):
Everyone should strive
Until the goal is achieved.
When the goal is achieved,
One shines brilliantly.
There is nothing better
Than patience.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 11.8

item.title: Prince, having heard Brahmā's request, out of compassion for beings, I surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye. With the Buddha-eye, Prince, I saw beings with…
item.description:
Prince, having heard Brahmā's request, out of compassion for beings, I surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye. With the Buddha-eye, Prince, I saw beings with little dust in their eyes, with much dust in their eyes, with keen faculties, with dull faculties, with good qualities, with bad qualities, easy to teach, hard to teach, and some who saw the danger in future rebirth and in faulty actions. Just as in a pond of blue lotuses, red lotuses, or white lotuses, some lotuses are born in the water, grow in the water, do not rise above the water, thrive while submerged; some lotuses are born in the water, grow in the water, live reaching the water's surface; some lotuses are born in the water, grow in the water, rise above the water and stand without being wetted by the water. So too, Prince, with the Buddha-eye I saw beings with little dust in their eyes... And, Prince, I spoke this verse to Brahmā Sahampati:

The door to the Deathless is open,
For those who are willing to hear.
Renounce your inaccurate faith.
Thinking of the trouble,
I did not want to teach
The supreme sublime Dhamma
Among humans.
(O Brahmā)

From: Majjhima Nikāya 85 – Bodhirājakumārasutta

item.title: And, Mahānāma, how is a noble disciple possessed of virtue? Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple is virtuous, he lives restrained by the restraint of the…
item.description:
And, Mahānāma, how is a noble disciple possessed of virtue? Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple is virtuous, he lives restrained by the restraint of the Pātimokkha, perfect in conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults, undertaking and training in the training rules. Mahānāma, thus is a noble disciple possessed of virtue.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 53 – Sekhasutta

item.title: Four Right Efforts: Here, friends, a bhikkhu generates desire, strives, arouses energy, applies his mind, and exerts his mind for the non-arising of unarisen evil,…
item.description:
Four Right Efforts: Here, friends, a bhikkhu generates desire, strives, arouses energy, applies his mind, and exerts his mind for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states. He generates desire, strives, arouses energy, applies his mind, and exerts his mind for the abandoning of arisen evil, unwholesome states. He generates desire, strives, arouses energy, applies his mind, and exerts his mind for the arising of unarisen wholesome states. He generates desire, strives, arouses energy, applies his mind, and exerts his mind for the maintenance, non-confusion, increase, expansion, cultivation, and fulfillment of arisen wholesome states.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 33 – Saṅgītisutta

item.title: Elder Mahānāga: Those who have no respect for fellow celibates — They decline in the true Dhamma, like fish in shallow water. Those who have…
item.description:
Elder Mahānāga:

Those who have no respect for fellow celibates —
They decline in the true Dhamma, like fish in shallow water.

Those who have no respect for fellow celibates —
They do not grow in the true Dhamma, like rotten seed in a field.

Those who have no respect for fellow celibates —
They are far from Nibbāna, in the teaching of the Dhamma King.

Those who have respect for fellow celibates —
They do not decline in the true Dhamma, like fish in abundant water.

Those who have respect for fellow celibates —
They grow in the true Dhamma, like good seed in a field.

Those who have respect for fellow celibates —
They are close to Nibbāna, in the teaching of the Dhamma King.

From: Theragāthā 6.3

item.title: Here, bhikkhus, with my mind I know the mind of a person with evil intent thus: 'If this person were to die at this moment,…
item.description:
Here, bhikkhus, with my mind I know the mind of a person with evil intent thus: 'If this person were to die at this moment, he would be placed in hell as surely as if carried there.' Why is that? Because his mind is evil. Bhikkhus, it is because of an evil mind that some beings, at the breaking up of the body, are reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell.

Knowing the evil mind
Of a person here,
The Buddha, among bhikkhus,
Spoke this meaning.

If that person should die at this very moment,
He would be reborn in hell,
Because his mind is evil.

Just as one takes what one carries
And is placed accordingly,
So it is accordingly
Because of an evil mind,
Beings go to an evil destination.

From: Itivuttaka 20

item.title: Furthermore, Lohicca, there is here a teacher who has not attained the goal of the ascetic life for the sake of which one goes forth…
item.description:
Furthermore, Lohicca, there is here a teacher who has not attained the goal of the ascetic life for the sake of which one goes forth from home to homelessness. Not having attained that goal, he teaches Dhamma to his disciples: 'This is for your good! This is for your happiness!' Those disciples listen to his words, lend ear, apply their minds to understanding, and live not contrary to the teacher's teaching. Such a teacher should be censured: 'The Venerable One has not attained the goal of the ascetic life for the sake of which he went forth. Not having attained that goal, he teaches Dhamma to his disciples, saying "This is for your good! This is for your happiness!" Those disciples listen to him, lend ear, apply their minds to understanding, yet live contrary to the teacher's teaching. Like a person who abandons his own melon patch and thinks about weeding another's field. I say that such conduct is evil and greedy, for who would do work for another?' Lohicca, this is the second kind of teacher worthy of criticism, and whoever criticizes such a teacher criticizes rightly, properly, and without fault.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 12 – Lohiccasutta

item.title: 'This is wholesome', 'this is unwholesome' has been well explained by the Blessed One. 'This is blameworthy', 'this is blameless', 'this should be practiced', 'this…
item.description:
'This is wholesome', 'this is unwholesome' has been well explained by the Blessed One. 'This is blameworthy', 'this is blameless', 'this should be practiced', 'this should be avoided', 'this is low', 'this is sublime', 'this is the equal pairing of dark and bright' has been well explained by the Blessed One. A teacher who has well explained wholesome and unwholesome states, blameworthy and blameless states, what should be practiced and what should be avoided, low and sublime, the equal pairing of dark and bright, a teacher endowed with such qualities is hard to find in the past or present except the Blessed One. The path leading to Nibbāna for disciples, and Nibbāna itself, have been well explained by the Blessed One as coalescing into one, like the water of the Ganges river flowing and merging with the water of the Yamunā. So too, the path leading to Nibbāna for disciples, and Nibbāna itself, have been well explained by the Blessed One as coalescing into one. A teacher who has thus well explained the path leading to Nibbāna, a teacher endowed with such qualities, is hard to find in the past or present except the Blessed One.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 19 – Mahāgovindasutta
